In mathematics, especially [[category theory]], '''Joyal's theta category''' <math>\Theta</math> is an alternative to the [[simplex category]] <math>\Delta</math>. It was introduced by [[André Joyal]] to give a definition of an [[∞-category]] using <math>\Theta</math>-sets  = [[Presheaf (category theory)|presheaves]] on <math>\Theta</math> instead of [[simplicial set]]s = presheaves on <math>\Delta</math>. Namely, in the definition of Boardman and Vogt (which is the standard definition today), an ∞-category is defined as a simplicial set satisfying the weak Kan condition. In a similar way, Joyal proposed to define an ∞-category as a <math>\Theta</math>-set satisfying the weak Kan condition.<ref>{{harvnb|Joyal|1997|loc=§ 1.3. Definition 2.}}</ref>

In practice, the category <math>\Theta</math> is often used to define [[(∞, n)-category|(∞, n)-categories]].
